title: action bash
desc: The action bash command specifies a Bash shell command to be run when an event handler is triggered.

title: alias
cmd:
alias alias_name command_name
no alias alias_name
default alias alias_name
desc: The alias command creates an alias for a CLI command.

title: bash
desc: The bash command starts the Linux Bash shell.

title: comment (various configuration modes)
cmd:
comment comment_text EOF
no comment
default comment !! comment_text
desc: The comment command adds a comment for the active configuration mode to running-config.

title: configure (configure terminal)
desc: The configure command places the switch in the Global Configuration mode to configure features at the system level.

title: configure checkpoint
desc: The configure checkpoint command saves the running configuration to a checkpoint file.

title: configure convert
desc: The configure convert command converts the current configuration syntax to the specified syntax.

title: configure network
desc: The configure network command is deprecated.

title: copy running-config
desc: The current operating configuration of the switch is stored in a virtual file called running-config.

title: daemon
cmd:
daemon daemon_name
no daemon daemon_name
default daemon daemon_name
desc: The daemon command accesses daemon configuration mode for adding or removing external daemons and scripts, which are then managed by ProcMgr.

title: delay
desc: The delay command specifies the time in seconds the system will delay between a triggering event and the execution of an event handler action.

title: dir
desc: The dir command displays a list of files on a file system.

title: disable
desc: The disable command exchanges the session’s current command mode with the specified privilege level.

title: enable
desc: The enable command places the switch in Privileged EXEC mode.

title: event-handler DropCountersHandler
cmd:
event-handler DropCountersHandler
no event-handler DropCountersHandler
default event-handler DropCountersHandler
desc: The event-handler DropCountersHandler command enables the adverse drop counters monitor with event handlers.

title: event-handler
cmd:
event-handler name
no event-handler name
default event-handler name
desc: An event handler executes a Linux Bash shell command in response to a specific system event.

title: ip ftp client source-interface
cmd:
ip ftp [client] source-interface INTERFACE [vrf vrf_name]
no ip ftp [client] source-interface
default ip ftp [client] source-interface
desc: By default, the FTP (File Transfer Protocol) source IP address is selected by the switch (the IP address of the source interface if one is assigned).

title: ip http client local-interface
cmd:
ip http client local-interface INTERFACE [vrf vrf_name]
no ip http client local-interface
default ip http client local-interface
desc: The ip http client local-interface command specifies the source IP address for hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP) connections.

title: ip ssh client source-interface
cmd:
ip ssh [client] source-interface INTERFACE [vrf vrf_name]
no ip ssh [client] source-interface
default ip ssh [client] source-interface
desc: The ip ssh client source-interface command specifies the source IP address for secure shell (SSH) connections.

title: ip tftp client source-interface
cmd:
ip tftp [client] source-interface INTERFACE [vrf vrf_name]
no ip tftp [client] source-interface
default ip tftp [client] source-interface
desc: The ip tftp client source-interface command specifies the source IP address for Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) connections.

title: platform arad lag mode

platform sand fabric mode [MODE_SETTING]

platform sand forwarding mode [MODE_SETTING]
no platform sand forwarding mode
default platform sand forwarding mode
desc: The platform sand forwarding mode command specifies the forwarding compatibility mode under which the switch operates after the next system reload.

title: platform sand lag hardware-only

platform sand lag hardware-only
no platform sand lag hardware-only
default platform sand lag hardware-only
desc: The platform sand lag hardware-only command specifies that all LAGs will use hardware resources including single member LAGs.

title: platform sand lag mode
desc: The platform sand lag mode configures two Link Aggregation Groups (LAG) partitions, Partition A and Partition B, to support twice as many available Port Channels.

title: pwd
desc: The pwd command displays the working directory.

title: schedule config
desc: The schedule config command sets configuration parameters to the CLI scheduler.

schedule schedule_name PERIOD {max-log-files count | timeout timeout_interval}{command cmd | logging
verbose | loglocation flash:}
no schedule schedule_name

title: show (various configuration modes)
desc: The show command, when executed within a configuration mode, can display data in running-config for the active configuration mode.

title: show event-handler DropCountersHandler
desc: The show event-handler command displays details of the DropCountersHandler event handler.

title: show event-handler
desc: The show event-handler command displays the contents and activation history of a specified event handler or all event handlers.

title: show module
desc: The show module command displays information that identifies the supervisor, fabric, and linecard modules in a modular switch, including model number, serial number, hardware version number, software version

title: show platform sand compatibility
desc: The show sand platform compatibility command displays the fabric and forwarding modes.

title: show platform sand lag hardware-only
desc: The show platform sand lag hardware-only command displays whether or not LAGs are hardware-only.

title: show schedule
desc: The show schedule command displays logging output on the terminal during the current terminal session.

title: show version
desc: The show version command displays information that identifies the switch, including its model number, serial number, and system MAC address.

title: terminal length
cmd:
terminal length lines
no terminal length
default terminal length
desc: The terminal length command overrides automatic pagination and sets pagination length for all show commands on a terminal.

title: terminal monitor

terminal monitor
no terminal monitor
default terminal monitor

title: trigger
desc: The trigger command specifies what event will trigger the event handler.

title: Boot Loader Aboot
desc: Aboot is the boot loader for Arista switches.

title: boot-config
desc: The boot-config file is an ASCII file that Aboot uses to configure console communication settings, locate the EOS flash image, and specify initial network configuration settings.

title: boot-config File Structure
desc: Each line in the boot-config file specifies a configuration setting and has this format: NAME=VALUE • NAME is the parameter label.

title: boot-config Command Line Content
desc: Aboot configuration commands that boot-config files can contain include: • SWI specifies the location and file name of the EOS image file that Aboot loads when booting, using the same format as the boot command to designate a local or network path.

title: running-config
desc: The running-config is a virtual file that contains the system’s operating configuration, formatted as a command sequence.

title: startup-config
desc: The startup-config file is stored in flash memory and contains the configuration the switch loads when booting.

title: Redundancy Supervisor Protocols
desc: There are three available supervisor redundancy protocols.

title: System Reset
desc: When a reset condition exists, Aboot can either reset the switch without user intervention or facilitate a manual reset through the Aboot shell.

title: CONSOLESPEED
desc: The CONSOLESPEED command in the boot-config file specifies the console baud rate when the switch is booted.

title: NET Commands
desc: Aboot uses NET commands in the boot-config file during switch booting to configure the network interface used for switch configuration.

title: install bios source
cmd: install bios source SOURCE [active | standby] [reload | now]
desc: install bios source command is used to install an Aboot Update File (AUF) to upgrade Aboot firmware.

title: PASSWORD (ABOOT)
desc: PASSWORD specifies the Aboot password, as described in Accessing the Aboot Shell.

title: SWI
desc: SWI specifies the location and file name of the EOS image file that Aboot loads when booting, using the same format as boot-config to designate a local or network path.

title: boot console
desc: The boot console command configures terminal settings for serial devices connecting to the console port.

title: boot secret
cmd:
boot secret [ENCRYPT_TYPE] password
no boot secret
default boot secret

title: sFlow
desc: This chapter describes Arista's implementation of sFlow, including configuration instructions and command descriptions.

title: sFlow Conceptual Overview
desc: Sampled Flow Tracking Commands

title: sFlow Technology
desc: Sampled Flow (sFlow) provides a multi-vendor sampling technology that continuously monitors application level traffic flow at wire speed simultaneously on all interfaces.

title: sFlow Agents
desc: The sFlow agent runs a software process as part of the network management software within an Arista switch.

title: sFlow Collector
desc: An sFlow collector runs software that analyzes and reports network traffic.

title: sFlow Data
desc: The sFlow Agent uses two forms of sampling: statistical packet-based sampling of switched flows and timebased sampling of network interface statistics.

title: sFlow and Mirroring
desc: sFlow and Mirroring supports using the same interface for a mirroring session and sFlow at the same time.

title: sFlow Subinterfaces

title: mgmt commit check
desc: System — This command validates the configuration but does not apply them to the Running DB.

title: mgmt delete-config XPATH
desc: System — This command uses a SET_CONFIG request (with delete option) over the MGMT Frontend Interface o delete the YANG data node at the given xpath unless it is a key-leaf node(in which case it is not deleted).

title: mgmt load-config FILE <merge|replace>
desc: System — This command loads configuration in JSON format from the filepath specified, and merges or replaces the Candidate DB as per the option specified.

title: mgmt rollback commit-id WORD
desc: System — This command rolls back the Running Database contents to the state corresponding to the commit-id specified.

title: mgmt rollback last WORD
desc: System — This command rolls back the last specified number of recent commits.

title: mgmt save-config <candidate|running> FILE
desc: System — This command dumps the DB specified in the db-name into the file in JSON format.

title: mgmt set-config XPATH VALUE
desc: System — This command uses a SET_CONFIG request over the MGMT Frontend Interface for the specified xpath with specific value.

title: show mgmt backend-adapter all
desc: System — This command shows the backend adapter information and the clients/daemons connected to the adapters.

title: show mgmt backend-yang-xpath-registry
desc: System — This command shows which Backend adapters are registered for which YANG data subtree(s).

title: show mgmt commit-history
desc: System — This command dumps details of upto last 10 commits handled by MGMTd.

title: show mgmt datastore-contents [candidate|operation|running] [xpath WORD] [file WORD] json|xml
cmd: show mgmt datastore-contents candidate xpath MYWORD file MYWORD json|xml
desc: System — This command dumps the subtree pointed by the xpath in JSON or XML format. If filepath is not present then the tree will be printed on the shell.

title: show mgmt frontend-adapter all [detail]
desc: System — This command shows the frontend adapter information and the clients connected to the adapters.

title: show mgmt get-data [candidate|operation|running] XPATH
desc: System — This command uses the GET_DATA operation over the MGMT Frontend interface and returns the xpaths and values of the nodes of the subtree pointed by the <xpath>.

title: show mgmt transaction all

title: [no] debug pim zebra
desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — This gathers data about events from zebra that come up through the ZAPI.

title: autorp announce A.B.C.D [A.B.C.D/M | group-list PREFIX_LIST]
desc: Multicast — Configure the router to advertise itself as a candidate PIM-SM RP via AutoRP. The supported groups can be defined as a single group range, or multiple group ranges can be defined via a prefix list.

title: autorp announce {scope (1-255) | interval (1-65535) | holdtime (0-65535)}
desc: Multicast — Configure the AutoRP advertise messages. The scope defines the TTL value in the messages to limit the scope, defaults to 31.

title: autorp send-rp-discovery [source <address A.B.C.D | interface IFNAME | loopback | any>]
desc: Multicast — Enable the AutoRP mapping agent on this router. The mapping agent listens for candidate RP announcements, aggregates them, and sends AutoRP discovery messages so other routers can learn RP information dynamically.

title: autorp send-rp-discovery {scope (0-255) | interval (1-65535) | holdtime (0-65535)}
desc: Multicast — Configure AutoRP mapping agent discovery messages. The scope defines the TTL value in the messages to limit the scope, defaults to 31.

title: bsr candidate-bsr [priority (0-255)] [source [address A.B.C.D] | [interface INTERFACE] | [loopback] | [any]]
cmd: bsr candidate-bsr priority 10 [source address 10.0.0.1 | interface eth0 | loopback | any]
desc: Multicast — Configure the router to advertise itself as a candidate PIM-SM BSR. The candidate with the highest priority becomes the BSR for the domain (high wins).

title: bsr candidate-rp [interval]
desc: Multicast — Configure the router to advertise itself as a candidate PIM-SM RP at the specified interval in seconds.

title: bsr candidate-rp [priority (0-255)] [source [address A.B.C.D] | [interface INTERFACE] | [loopback] | [any]]
cmd: bsr candidate-rp priority 10 [source address 10.0.0.1 | interface eth0 | loopback | any]
desc: Multicast — Configure the router to advertise itself as a candidate PIM-SM RP. interval can be used to configure the interval in seconds to send these advertisements.

title: bsr candidate-rp group A.B.C.D/M
desc: Multicast — Configure the multicast group prefix that this candidate RP advertises itself for.

title: clear ip pim [vrf NAME] interfaces
cmd: clear ip pim vrf MYNAME interfaces
desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — Reset PIM interfaces.

title: clear ip pim [vrf NAME] oil
cmd: clear ip pim vrf MYNAME oil
desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — Rescan PIM OIL (output interface list).

desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — This turns on debugging for IGMP protocol activity.

title: debug mroute

title: debug mtrace
desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — This turns on debugging for mtrace protocol activity.

title: debug pim autorp
desc: Multicast — This turns on debugging for PIM AutoRP protocol events.

title: debug pim bsm
desc: Multicast · ✓ doc + live (Docker FRR) — This turns on debugging for BSR message processing.

title: debug pim graft
desc: Multicast — This turns on debugging for PIM graft message processing. Graft messages are similar to PIM joins but are specifically used for PIM dense mode.

title: debug pim packet-dump
desc: Multicast — This turns on an extraordinary amount of data. Each pim packet sent and received is dumped for debugging purposes.

title: debug pim state-refresh
desc: Multicast — This turns on debugging for PIM state-refresh message processing. State-refresh messages are used in PIM dense mode.

title: ecmp
desc: Multicast — If PIM has the a choice of ECMP nexthops for a particular RPF, PIM will cause S,G flows to be spread out amongst the nexthops.

title: ecmp rebalance
desc: Multicast — If PIM is using ECMP and an interface goes down, cause PIM to rebalance all S,G flows across the remaining nexthops.

title: ip igmp
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM to receive IGMP reports and Query on this interface. The default version is v3.

title: ip igmp access-list ACCESSLIST4_NAME
desc: Multicast — Apply the indicated access list to filter incoming IGMP joins.

title: ip igmp generate-query-once [version (2-3)]
desc: Multicast — Generate IGMP query (v2/v3) on user requirement. This will not depend on the existing IGMP general query timer.

title: ip igmp immediate-leave
desc: Multicast — Immediately leaves an IGMP group when receiving a IGMPv2 Leave packet.

title: ip igmp join-group A.B.C.D [A.B.C.D]
desc: Multicast — Join multicast group or source-group on an interface. This will result in an IGMP join happening through a local socket so that IGMP reports will be sent on this interface.

title: ip igmp last-member-query-count (1-255)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP last member query count. The default value is the currently configured robustness value.

title: ip igmp last-member-query-interval (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP last member query interval in deciseconds. The default value is 10 deciseconds.

title: ip igmp max-groups (0-4294967295)
desc: Multicast — Set the maximum number of IGMP groups that the can be joined on an interface.

title: ip igmp max-sources (0-4294967295)
desc: Multicast — Set the maximum number of IGMP sources to learn per group.

title: ip igmp proxy
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM to send proxy IGMP reports for joins occurring on all other interfaces on this interface.

title: ip igmp proxy route-map ROUTE-MAP
desc: Multicast — Apply a route-map to filter which multicast (S,G) entries are forwarded via IGMP proxy on this interface.

title: ip igmp query-interval (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP query interval that PIM will use.

title: ip igmp query-max-response-time (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP query response timeout value. If an report is not returned in the specified time we will assume the S,G or \*,G has timed out.

title: ip igmp require-router-alert
desc: Multicast — Only accept IGMP reports with the router-alert IP option.

title: ip igmp robustness (1-255)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP robustness value. The default value is 2.

title: ip igmp route-map ROUTE-MAP
desc: Multicast — Apply the indicated route map to filter incoming IGMP joins. The following match statements can be used: * match ip multicast-group A.B.C.D * match ip multicast-group prefix-list IPV4-PREFIX-LIST * match ip multicast-so…

title: ip igmp static-group A.B.C.D [A.B.C.D]
desc: Multicast — Add a static multicast group or source-group on an interface. This will behave as if there is a receiver on this interface without any IGMP reports.

title: ip igmp version (2-3)
desc: Multicast — Set the IGMP version used on this interface. The default value is 3.

title: ip igmp watermark-warn (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — Configure watermark warning generation for an IGMP group limit. Generates a warning once the configured group limit is reached while adding new groups.

title: ip mroute INTERFACE A.B.C.D [A.B.C.D]
desc: Multicast — Set a static multicast route for a traffic coming on the current interface to be forwarded on the given interface if the traffic matches the group address and optionally the source address.

title: ip mroute PREFIX NEXTHOP [DISTANCE]
desc: Multicast — Adds a static route entry to the Multicast RIB. This performs exactly as the ip route command, except that it inserts the route in the Multicast RIB instead of the Unicast RIB.

title: ip multicast boundary ACCESS-LIST
desc: Multicast — Set a PIM multicast boundary, based upon the ACCESS-LIST. If a PIM join or IGMP report is received on this interface and the (S,G) tuple is denied by the access-list, PIM will ignore the join or report.

title: ip multicast boundary oil WORD
desc: Multicast — Set a PIM multicast boundary, based upon the WORD prefix-list. If a PIM join or IGMP report is received on this interface and the group is denied by the prefix-list, PIM will ignore the join or report.

title: ip pim [sm | dm | sm-dm]
desc: Multicast — Enable PIM on this interface. PIM will use this interface to form PIM neighborships and start exchanging PIM protocol messages with those neighbors.

title: ip pim active-active
desc: Multicast — Turn on PIM active-active configuration for a Vxlan interface. This command will not do anything if you do not have the underlying ability of a MLAG implementation.

title: ip pim allow-rp [rp-list PLIST]
desc: Multicast — When processing a (\*,G) source list entry for a particular group in a Join message, RFC 7761 dictates that the source address must be set to the RP address.

title: ip pim allowed-neighbors prefix-list PREFIX_LIST
desc: Multicast — Only establish sessions with PIM neighbors allowed by the prefix-list.

title: ip pim assert-interval (1000-86400000)
desc: Multicast — Modify the PIM assert interval in milliseconds on this interface (defaults to 18000).

title: ip pim assert-override-interval (1000-86400000)
desc: Multicast — Modify the PIM assert override interval in milliseconds on this interface (defaults to 3000).

title: ip pim bsm
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM that we would like to use this interface to process bootstrap messages.

title: ip pim dm prefix-list PREFIX_LIST
desc: Multicast — Limit dense mode multicast to the range configured with prefix-list. By default there is no limit.

title: ip pim drpriority (0-4294967295)
desc: Multicast — Set the DR Priority for the interface. This command is useful to allow the user to influence what node becomes the DR for a LAN segment.

title: ip pim hello (1-65535) (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — Set the PIM hello and hold interval for an interface.

title: ip pim join-prune-interval (5-600)
desc: Multicast — Modify the join/prune interval that PIM uses on this interface. Defaults to the globally configured value (which in turn defaults to 60 seconds).

title: ip pim override-interval (0-65535)
desc: Multicast — Modify the PIM LAN prune delay override interval in milliseconds on this interface (defaults to 2500).

title: ip pim passive
desc: Multicast — Disable sending and receiving PIM control packets on the interface.

title: ip pim ssm prefix-list PREFIX_LIST
desc: Multicast — Configure the Source-Specific-Multicast group range. Defaults to 232.0.0.0/8.

title: ip pim unicast-bsm
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM that we would like to allow interface to process unicast bootstrap messages.

title: ip pim use-source A.B.C.D
desc: Multicast — If you have multiple addresses configured on a particular interface and would like PIM to use a specific source address associated with that interface.

title: join-filter route-map RMAP_NAME
desc: Multicast — Specify a route-map name to use for filtering incoming PIM joins. The following route-map match statements can be used: * match ip multicast-group A.B.C.D * match ip multicast-group prefix-list IPV4-PREFIX-LIST * match…

title: join-prune-interval (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — :daemon: pim Modify the join/prune interval that PIM uses to the new value. Time is specified in seconds.

title: keep-alive-timer (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — :daemon: pim Modify the timeout value for an S,G flow from 1-65535 seconds. If choosing a value below 31 seconds be aware that some hardware platforms cannot see data flowing in better than 30 second chunks.

title: msdp mesh-group WORD member A.B.C.D
desc: Multicast — Create or update a mesh group to include the specified MSDP peer.

title: msdp mesh-group WORD source A.B.C.D
desc: Multicast — Create or update a mesh group to set the source address used to connect to peers.

title: msdp originator-id A.B.C.D
desc: Multicast — Use the specified originator ID instead of the multicast RP group.

title: msdp peer A.B.C.D password WORD
desc: Multicast — Use MD5 authentication to connect with the remote peer.

title: msdp peer A.B.C.D sa-filter ACL_NAME <in|out>
desc: Multicast — Configure incoming or outgoing SA filtering rule.

title: msdp peer A.B.C.D sa-limit <AMOUNT>
desc: Multicast — Configure the maximum number of SAs to learn from peer.

title: msdp peer A.B.C.D source A.B.C.D [as AS_NUMBER]
desc: Multicast — Create a regular MSDP session with peer using the specified source address. Optionally the Autonomous Number (AS) can be provided for eBGP assisted loop detection (see RFC 4611 Section 2.1.

title: msdp shutdown
desc: Multicast — Shutdown the MSDP sessions in this PIM instance.

title: msdp timers (1-65535) (1-65535) [(1-65535)]
desc: Multicast — Configure global MSDP timers. First value is the keep-alive interval.

title: mtrace A.B.C.D [A.B.C.D]
desc: Multicast — Display multicast traceroute towards source, optionally for particular group.

title: no autorp discovery
desc: Multicast — In order to use PIM, it is necessary to configure an RP for join messages to be sent to.

title: packets (1-255)
desc: Multicast — :daemon: pim When processing packets from a neighbor process the number of packets incoming at one time before moving on to the next task.

title: register-accept-list PLIST
desc: Multicast — When PIM receives a register packet the source of the packet will be compared to the prefix-list specified, PLIST, and if a permit is received normal processing continues.

title: register-suppress-time (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — :daemon: pim Modify the time that a FHR will suppress sending register messages to the RP.

title: router pim [vrf NAME]
desc: Multicast — Configure the global PIM protocol. To configure the PIM instance for a VRF, specify the VRF name.

title: rp A.B.C.D A.B.C.D/M
desc: Multicast — In order to use PIM, it is necessary to configure an RP for join messages to be sent to.

title: rp keep-alive-timer (1-65535)
desc: Multicast — :daemon: pim Modify the timeout value for an S,G flow from 1-65535 seconds at RP.

title: rpf-lookup-mode MODE [group-list PREFIX_LIST] [source-list PREFIX_LIST]
cmd: rpf-lookup-mode MODE group-list PREFIX_LIST source-list PREFIX_LIST
desc: Multicast — MODE sets the method used to perform RPF lookups. Supported modes: urib-only Performs the lookup on the Unicast RIB.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface>
desc: Interfaces — **Enable Babel routing on the specified interface.** The system immediately begins sending and receiving Babel packets on this interface.

title: set protocols babel parameters diversity
desc: Routing — **Enable radio-frequency diversity routing for the Babel process.** Enabling this feature is highly recommended for networks with many wireless nodes.

title: set protocols babel parameters diversity-factor <1-256>
desc: Routing — **Configure the multiplicative factor for diversity routing, in units of 1/256.** Lower multiplicative factors give greater weight to diversity in route selection.

title: set protocols babel parameters resend-delay <20-655340>
desc: Routing — **Configure the delay in milliseconds before the system resends an important request or update.** The default value is 2000 ms.

title: set protocols babel parameters smoothing-half-life <0-65534>
desc: Routing — **Configure the time constant, in seconds, for the smoothing algorithm used to implement hysteresis.** Higher values reduce route oscillation but slightly increase convergence time.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> type <auto|wired|wireless>
desc: Wireless — **Configure the network type for the Babel-enabled interface.** Choose from the following: * auto: Babel automatically detects if an interface is wired or wireless.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> split-horizon <default|disable|enable>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the split-horizon routing behavior for the specified interface.** Use one of the following options: * default: Babel automatically enables split-horizon on wired interfaces and disables it on wireless interf…

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> hello-interval <20-655340>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the interval, in milliseconds, between scheduled hello messages on the specified interface.** On wired links, Babel detects link failures within two hello intervals.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> update-interval <20-655340>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the interval, in milliseconds, between scheduled routing updates on the specified interface.** Because Babel uses triggered updates extensively, you can increase this value on reliable links with minimal pac…

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> rxcost <1-65534>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the base receive cost for the specified interface.** Babel applies this value based on the configured network type: * wired: The value is the routing cost advertised to neighboring routers.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> rtt-decay <1-256>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the decay factor for the exponential moving average of RTT samples, in units of 1/256.** Higher values discard older samples faster.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> rtt-min <1-65535>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the minimum RTT, in milliseconds, at which the cost to a neighbor begins to increase.** The additional cost is linear in (rtt - rtt-min).

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> rtt-max <1-65535>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the maximum RTT, in milliseconds, above which the cost to a neighbor stops increasing.** The default value is 120 ms.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> max-rtt-penalty <0-65535>
desc: Interfaces — **Configure the maximum cost added to a neighbor when RTT meets or exceeds rtt-max.** Setting this value to 0 disables RTT-based costs.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> enable-timestamps
desc: Interfaces — **Configure adding timestamps to each Hello and IHU message to calculate RTT values.** Enabling timestamps is recommended for tunnel interfaces.

title: set protocols babel interface <interface> channel <1-254|interfering|noninterfering>

desc: Multicast — Modify the join/prune interval that PIM uses to the new value. Time is specified in seconds.

title: set protocols pim keep-alive-timer <n>
desc: Multicast — Modify the time out value for a S,G flow from 1-65535 seconds. If choosing a value below 31 seconds be aware that some hardware platforms cannot see data flowing in better than 30 second chunks.

title: set protocols pim packets <n>
desc: Multicast — When processing packets from a neighbor process the number of packets incoming at one time before moving on to the next task.

title: set protocols pim register-accept-list <prefix-list>
desc: Multicast — When PIM receives a register packet the source of the packet will be compared to the prefix-list specified, and if a permit is received normal processing continues.

title: set protocols pim register-suppress-time <n>
desc: Multicast — Modify the time that pim will register suppress a FHR will send register notifications to the kernel.

title: set protocols pim rp <address> group <group>
desc: Multicast — In order to use PIM, it is necessary to configure a RP (Rendezvous Point) for join messages to be sent to.

title: set protocols pim rp keep-alive-timer <n>
desc: Multicast — Modify the time out value for a S,G flow from 1-65535 seconds at RP (Rendezvous Point).

title: set protocols pim no-v6-secondary
desc: Multicast — When sending PIM hello packets tell PIM to not send any v6 secondary addresses on the interface.

title: set protocols pim spt-switchover infinity-and-beyond [prefix-list <list>]
desc: Multicast — On the last hop router if it is desired to not switch over to the SPT tree configure this command.

title: set protocols pim ssm prefix-list <list>
desc: Multicast — Specify a range of group addresses via a prefix-list that forces PIM to never do SSM (Source-Specific Multicast) over.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> bfd [profile <name>]
desc: Multicast — Automatically create BFD session for each RIP peer discovered in this interface.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> dr-priority <n>
desc: Multicast — Set the DR (Designated Router) Priority for the interface. This command is useful to allow the user to influence what node becomes the DR for a LAN segment.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> hello <n>
desc: Multicast — Set the PIM hello and hold interval for a interface.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> no-bsm
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM that we would not like to use this interface to process bootstrap messages.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> no-unicast-bsm
desc: Multicast — Tell PIM that we would not like to use this interface to process unicast bootstrap messages.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> passive
desc: Multicast — Disable sending and receiving PIM control packets on the interface.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> source-address <ip-address>
desc: Multicast — If you have multiple addresses configured on a particular interface and would like PIM to use a specific source address associated with that interface.

title: set protocols pim igmp watermark-warning <n>
desc: Multicast — Configure watermark warning generation for an IGMP group limit. Generates warning once the configured group limit is reached while adding new groups.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp join <multicast-address> source-address <IP-…
cmd: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp join <multicast-address> source-address <IP-address>
desc: Multicast — Use this command to allow the selected interface to join a multicast group defining the multicast address you want to join and the source IP address too.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp query-interval <seconds>
cmd: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp query-interval <seconds>
desc: Multicast — Use this command to configure in the selected interface the IGMP host query interval (1-1800) in seconds that PIM will use.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp query-max-response-time <n>
cmd: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp query-max-response-time <n>
desc: Multicast — Use this command to configure in the selected interface the IGMP query response timeout value (10-250) in deciseconds.

title: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp version <version-number>
cmd: set protocols pim interface <interface> igmp version <version-number>
desc: Multicast — Use this command to define in the selected interface whether you choose IGMP version 2 or 3.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> next-hop <address>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the next-hop IP address for the specified source subnet.** When multicast traffic originates from this subnet, the router expects it to arrive from the upstream neighbor at the specified IP address.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> next-hop <address> distance <1-255>
cmd: set protocols static mroute <subnet> next-hop <address> distance <1-255>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the administrative distance for the mroute via the specified next-hop IP address.** Mroutes with a lower administrative distance are prioritized over mroutes with a higher distance.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> next-hop <address> disable
cmd: set protocols static mroute <subnet> next-hop <address> disable
desc: Multicast — **Disable the mroute via the specified next-hop IP address.** This command temporarily deactivates the mroute while preserving the configured subnet, next-hop, and distance parameters.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> interface <interface>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the valid interface for the specified source subnet.** When multicast traffic originates from this subnet, the router expects it to arrive on the specified interface.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> interface <interface> distance <1-255>
cmd: set protocols static mroute <subnet> interface <interface> distance <1-255>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the administrative distance for the mroute via the specified interface.** Mroutes with a lower administrative distance are prioritized over mroutes with a higher distance.

title: set protocols static mroute <subnet> interface <interface> disable
cmd: set protocols static mroute <subnet> interface <interface> disable
desc: Multicast — **Disable the mroute via the specified interface.** This command temporarily deactivates the mroute while preserving the configured subnet, interface, and distance parameters.

title: set protocols bfd peer <address>
desc: BFD — **Configure the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the BFD peer.** You can configure multiple BFD peers by specifying a different IP address for each neighbor you want to monitor.

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> echo-mode
desc: BFD — **Enable BFD echo transmission mode for the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> multihop
desc: BFD — **Configure the peer at the specified IP address as a multi-hop neighbor.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> source address <address>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> source address <address>
desc: BFD — **Configure the source IP address for the BFD session with the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> source interface <interface>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> source interface <interface>
desc: BFD — **Configure the source interface for the BFD session with the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval echo-interval <10-60000>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval echo-interval <10-60000>
desc: BFD — **Configure the minimum interval, in milliseconds, at which the local system can receive echo packets from the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval multiplier <2-255>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval multiplier <2-255>
desc: BFD — **Configure the detection multiplier for the peer at the specified IP address.** BFD multiplies the negotiated interval by this value to calculate the detection time — the period after which it declares the session down…

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval receive <10-60000>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval receive <10-60000>
desc: BFD — **Configure the interval, in milliseconds, at which the local system can receive BFD control packets from the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval transmit <10-60000>
cmd: set protocols bfd peer <address> interval transmit <10-60000>
desc: BFD — **Configure the interval, in milliseconds, at which you want the local system to transmit BFD control packets to the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> shutdown
desc: BFD — **Disable the BFD session with the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> minimum-ttl <1-254>
desc: BFD — **Configure the minimum TTL (Time to Live) value that incoming BFD control packets must have to be accepted from the peer at the specified IP address.** BFD discards any packet whose TTL is below this threshold.

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> passive
desc: BFD — **Configure the BFD session with the peer at the specified IP address to operate in passive mode.** In passive mode, the local system does not initiate the BFD session.

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> profile <profile>
desc: BFD — **Apply settings from a designated BFD profile to the peer at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bfd peer <address> vrf <vrf>
desc: BFD — **Bind the BFD session with the peer at the specified IP address to a specific VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) instance.**

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <neighbor> bfd
desc: BGP — **Enable BFD failure detection for the BGP session with the neighbor at the specified IP address.**

title: set protocols bgp peer-group <neighbor> bfd
desc: BGP — **Enable BFD failure detection for all neighbors in the specified BGP peer group.**

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> bfd
desc: OSPF — **Enable BFD failure detection for OSPF neighbors discovered on the specified interface.** When OSPF forms an adjacency with a neighbor on this interface, it requests BFD to establish a session with that neighbor.

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> bfd
desc: OSPFv3 — **Enable BFD failure detection for OSPFv3 neighbors discovered on the specified interface.** When OSPFv3 forms an adjacency with a neighbor on this interface, it requests BFD to establish a session with that neighbor.

title: set protocols isis interface <interface> bfd
desc: ISIS — **Enable BFD failure detection for IS-IS neighbors discovered on the specified interface.** When IS-IS forms an adjacency with a neighbor on this interface, it requests BFD to establish a session with that neighbor.

title: show bfd peers
desc: BFD — **Show all BFD peers.**

title: set protocols static route <subnet> next-hop <address> bfd multi-hop source-address <addr…
cmd: set protocols static route <subnet> next-hop <address> bfd multi-hop source-address <address>
desc: BFD — **Configure BFD failure detection for a multi-hop static route.** BFD uses the next-hop IP address as the BFD peer IP address and the multi-hop source IP address as the local source IP for outgoing BFD packets.

title: set protocols static route6 <subnet> next-hop <address> bfd multi-hop source-address <add…
cmd: set protocols static route6 <subnet> next-hop <address> bfd multi-hop source-address <address>
desc: BFD — **Configure BFD failure detection for a multi-hop IPv6 static route.** BFD uses the next-hop IPv6 address as the BFD peer IPv6 address and the multi-hop source IPv6 address as the local source IPv6 address for outgoing…

title: set protocols ospf area <number> network <A.B.C.D/M>
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the OSPF enabled interface(s). If the interface has an address from defined range then the command enables OSPF on this interface so router can provide network information to the other ospf router…

title: set protocols ospf auto-cost reference-bandwidth <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the reference bandwidth for cost calculations, where bandwidth can be in range from 1 to 4294967, specified in Mbits/s.

title: set protocols ospf parameters router-id <rid>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the router-ID of the OSPF process. The router-ID may be an IP address of the router, but need not be – it can be any arbitrary 32bit number.

title: set protocols ospf default-information originate [always] [metric <number>] [metric-type…
desc: OSPF — Originate an AS-External (type-5) LSA describing a default route into all external-routing capable areas, of the specified metric and metric type.

title: set protocols ospf distance global <distance>
desc: OSPF — This command change distance value of OSPF globally. The distance range is 1 to 255.

title: set protocols ospf distance ospf <external|inter-area|intra-area> <distance>
desc: OSPF — This command change distance value of OSPF. The arguments are the distance values for external routes, inter-area routes and intra-area routes respectively.

title: set protocols ospf log-adjacency-changes [detail]
desc: OSPF — This command allows to log changes in adjacency. With the optional detail argument, all changes in adjacency status are shown.

title: set protocols ospf max-metric router-lsa <administrative|on-shutdown <seconds>|on-startup…
desc: OSPF — This enables 3137 support, where the OSPF process describes its transit links in its router-LSA as having infinite distance so that other routers will avoid calculating transit paths through the router while still being…

title: set protocols ospf parameters abr-type <cisco|ibm|shortcut|standard>
desc: OSPF — This command selects ABR model. OSPF router supports four ABR models: **cisco** – a router will be considered as ABR if it has several configured links to the networks in different areas one of which is a backbone area.

title: set protocols ospf parameters rfc1583-compatibility
desc: OSPF — 2328, the successor to 1583, suggests according to section G.2 (changes) in section 16.4.1 a change to the path preference algorithm that prevents possible routing loops that were possible in the old version of OSPFv2.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> passive [disable]
desc: OSPF — This command specifies interface as passive. Passive interface advertises its address, but does not run the OSPF protocol (adjacencies are not formed and hello packets are not generated).

title: set protocols ospf passive-interface default
desc: OSPF — This command specifies all interfaces as passive by default. Because this command changes the configuration logic to a default passive; therefore, interfaces where router adjacencies are expected need to be configured w…

title: set protocols ospf maximum-paths <1-64>
desc: OSPF — Use this command to control the maximum number of equal cost paths to reach a specific destination.

title: set protocols ospf refresh timers <seconds>
desc: OSPF — The router automatically updates link-state information with its neighbors. Only an obsolete information is updated which age has exceeded a specific threshold.

title: set protocols ospf timers throttle spf <delay|initial-holdtime|max-holdtime> <seconds>
cmd: set protocols ospf timers throttle spf <delay|initial-holdtime|max-holdtime> <seconds>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the initial delay, the initial-holdtime and the maximum-holdtime between when SPF is calculated and the event which triggered the calculation.

title: set protocols ospf ldp-sync
desc: OSPF — This command will enable IGP-LDP synchronization globally for OSPF. This requires for LDP to be functional.

title: set protocols ospf ldp-sync holddown <seconds>
desc: OSPF — This command will change the hold down value globally for IGP-LDP synchronization during convergence/interface flap events.

title: set protocols ospf capability opaque
desc: OSPF — ospfd supports Opaque LSA 2370 as partial support for MPLS Traffic Engineering LSAs.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the area to be a Stub Area. That is, an area where no router originates routes external to OSPF and hence an area where all external routes are via the ABR(s).

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub no-summary
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub no-summary
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the area to be a Totally Stub Area. In addition to stub area limitations this area type prevents an ABR from injecting Network-Summary (type-3) LSAs into the specified stub area.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub default-cost <number>
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type stub default-cost <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the cost of default-summary LSAs announced to stubby areas. The cost range is 0 to 16777215.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the area to be a Not So Stubby Area. External routing information is imported into an NSSA in Type-7 LSAs.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa no-summary
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa no-summary
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the area to be a NSSA Totally Stub Area. ABRs for such an area do not need to pass Network-Summary (type-3) LSAs (except the default summary route), ASBR-Summary LSAs (type-4) and AS-External LSAs…

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa default-cost <number>
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa default-cost <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the default cost of LSAs announced to NSSA areas. The cost range is 0 to 16777215.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa translate <always|candidate|never>
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> area-type nssa translate <always|candidate|never>
desc: OSPF — Specifies whether this NSSA border router will unconditionally translate Type-7 LSAs into Type-5 LSAs.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> authentication plaintext-password
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> authentication plaintext-password
desc: OSPF — This command specifies that simple password authentication should be used for the given area.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> authentication md5
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> authentication md5
desc: OSPF — This command specify that OSPF packets must be authenticated with MD5 HMACs within the given area.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> range <A.B.C.D/M> [cost <number>]
desc: OSPF — This command summarizes intra area paths from specified area into one summary-LSA (Type-3) announced to other areas.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> range <A.B.C.D/M> not-advertise
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> range <A.B.C.D/M> not-advertise
desc: OSPF — This command instead of summarizing intra area paths filter them - i.e. intra area paths from this range are not advertised into other areas.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> export-list <acl_number>
desc: OSPF — Filter Type-3 summary-LSAs announced to other areas originated from intra- area paths from specified area.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> import-list <acl_number>
desc: OSPF — Same as export-list, but it applies to paths announced into specified area as Type-3 summary-LSAs.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> range <A.B.C.D/M> substitute <E.F.G.H/M>
cmd: set protocols ospf area <number> range <A.B.C.D/M> substitute <E.F.G.H/M>
desc: OSPF — One Type-3 summary-LSA with routing info <E.F.G.H/M> is announced into backbone area if defined area contains at least one intra-area network (i.e.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> shortcut <default|disable|enable>
desc: OSPF — This parameter allows to "shortcut" routes (non-backbone) for inter-area routes.

title: set protocols ospf area <number> virtual-link <A.B.C.D>
desc: OSPF — Provides a backbone area coherence by virtual link establishment. In general, OSPF protocol requires a backbone area (area 0) to be coherent and fully connected.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> area <x.x.x.x | x>
cmd: set protocols ospf interface <interface> area <x.x.x.x | x>
desc: OSPF — Enable ospf on an interface and set associated area. If you have a lot of interfaces, and/or a lot of subnets, then enabling OSPF via this command may result in a slight performance improvement.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> authentication plaintext-password <text>
cmd: set protocols ospf interface <interface> authentication plaintext-password <text>
desc: OSPF — This command sets OSPF authentication key to a simple password. After setting, all OSPF packets are authenticated.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> authentication md5 key-id <id> md5-key <text>
cmd: set protocols ospf interface <interface> authentication md5 key-id <id> md5-key <text>
desc: OSPF — This command specifys that MD5 HMAC authentication must be used on this interface.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> bandwidth <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets the interface bandwidth for cost calculations, where bandwidth can be in range from 1 to 100000, specified in Mbits/s.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> cost <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets link cost for the specified interface. The cost value is set to router-LSA’s metric field and used for SPF calculation.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> dead-interval <number>
desc: OSPF — Set number of seconds for router Dead Interval timer value used for Wait Timer and Inactivity Timer.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> hello-multiplier <number>
desc: OSPF — The hello-multiplier specifies how many Hellos to send per second, from 1 (every second) to 10 (every 100ms).

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> hello-interval <number>
desc: OSPF — Set number of seconds for Hello Interval timer value. Setting this value, Hello packet will be sent every timer value seconds on the specified interface.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> mtu-ignore
desc: OSPF — This command disables check of the MTU value in the OSPF DBD packets. Thus, use of this command allows the OSPF adjacency to reach the FULL state even though there is an interface MTU mismatch between two OSPF routers.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> network <type>
desc: OSPF — This command allows to specify the distribution type for the network connected to this interface: **broadcast** – broadcast IP addresses distribution.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> priority <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets Router Priority integer value. The router with the highest priority will be more eligible to become Designated Router.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> retransmit-interval <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets number of seconds for RxmtInterval timer value. This value is used when retransmitting Database Description and Link State Request packets if acknowledge was not received.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> transmit-delay <number>
desc: OSPF — This command sets number of seconds for InfTransDelay value. It allows to set and adjust for each interface the delay interval before starting the synchronizing process of the router's database with all neighbors.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> ldp-sync disable
cmd: set protocols ospf interface <interface> ldp-sync disable
desc: OSPF — This command disables IGP-LDP sync for this specific interface.

title: set protocols ospf interface <interface> ldp-sync holddown <seconds>
cmd: set protocols ospf interface <interface> ldp-sync holddown <seconds>
desc: OSPF — This command will change the hold down value for IGP-LDP synchronization during convergence/interface flap events, but for this interface only.

title: set protocols ospf aggregation timer <seconds>
desc: OSPF — Configure aggregation delay timer interval. Summarisation starts only after this delay timer expiry.

title: set protocols ospf summary-address x.x.x.x/y [tag (1-4294967295)]
desc: OSPF — This command enable/disables summarisation for the configured address range. Tag is the optional parameter.

title: set protocols ospf summary-address x.x.x.x/y no-advertise
cmd: set protocols ospf summary-address x.x.x.x/y no-advertise
desc: OSPF — This command to ensure not advertise the summary lsa for the matched external LSAs.

title: set protocols ospf graceful-restart [grace-period (1-1800)]
desc: OSPF — Configure Graceful Restart 3623 restarting support. When enabled, the default grace period is 120 seconds.

title: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper enable [router-id A.B.C.D]
cmd: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper enable [router-id A.B.C.D]
desc: OSPF — Configure Graceful Restart 3623 helper support. By default, helper support is disabled for all neighbours.

title: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper no-strict-lsa-checking
cmd: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper no-strict-lsa-checking
desc: OSPF — By default strict-lsa-checking is configured then the helper will abort the Graceful Restart when a LSA change occurs which affects the restarting router.

title: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper supported-grace-time
cmd: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper supported-grace-time
desc: OSPF — Supports as HELPER for configured grace period.

title: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper planned-only
cmd: set protocols ospf graceful-restart helper planned-only
desc: OSPF — It helps to support as HELPER only for planned restarts. By default, it supports both planned and unplanned outages.

title: set protocols ospf neighbor <A.B.C.D>
desc: BGP — This command specifies the IP address of the neighboring device.

title: set protocols ospf neighbor <A.B.C.D> poll-interval <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command specifies the length of time, in seconds, before the routing device sends hello packets out of the interface before it establishes adjacency with a neighbor.

title: set protocols ospf neighbor <A.B.C.D> priority <number>
desc: BGP — This command specifies the router priority value of the nonbroadcast neighbor associated with the IP address specified.

title: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source>
desc: OSPF — This command redistributes routing information from the given route source to the OSPF process.

title: set protocols ospf default-metric <number>
desc: OSPF — This command specifies the default metric value of redistributed routes. The metric range is 0 to 16777214.

title: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> metric <number>
cmd: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> metric <number>
desc: OSPF — This command specifies metric for redistributed routes from the given route source.

title: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> metric-type <1|2>
cmd: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> metric-type <1|2>
desc: OSPF — This command specifies metric type for redistributed routes. Difference between two metric types that metric type 1 is a metric which is "commensurable" with inner OSPF links.

title: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> route-map <name>
cmd: set protocols ospf redistribute <route source> route-map <name>
desc: OSPF — This command allows to use route map to filter redistributed routes from the given route source.

title: show ip ospf neighbor <A.B.C.D>
desc: BGP — This command displays the neighbors information in a detailed form for a neighbor whose IP address is specified.

title: show ip ospf neighbor <interface>
desc: BGP — This command displays the neighbors status for a neighbor on the specified interface.

title: show ip ospf interface [<interface>]
desc: OSPF — This command displays state and configuration of OSPF for the specified interface, or all interfaces if no interface is given.

title: show ip ospf route [detail]
desc: OSPF — This command displays the OSPF routing table, as determined by the most recent SPF calculation.

title: show ip ospf database <type> [A.B.C.D] [adv-router <A.B.C.D>|self-originate]
desc: OSPF — This command displays a database contents for a specific link advertisement type.

title: show ip ospf database max-age
desc: OSPF — This command displays LSAs in MaxAge list.

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> area <number>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command specifies the OSPFv3 enabled interface. This command is also used to enable the OSPF process.

title: set protocols ospfv3 parameters router-id <rid>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command sets the router-ID of the OSPFv3 process. The router-ID may be an IP address of the router, but need not be – it can be any arbitrary 32bit number.

title: set protocols ospfv3 distance global <distance>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command change distance value of OSPFv3 globally. The distance range is 1 to 255.

title: set protocols ospfv3 distance ospfv3 <external|inter-area|intra-area> <distance>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command change distance value of OSPFv3. The arguments are the distance values for external routes, inter-area routes and intra-area routes respectively.

title: set protocols ospfv3 area <number> range <prefix>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command summarizes intra area paths from specified area into one Type-3 Inter-Area Prefix LSA announced to other areas.

title: set protocols ospfv3 area <number> range <prefix> not-advertise
cmd: set protocols ospfv3 area <number> range <prefix> not-advertise
desc: OSPFv3 — This command instead of summarizing intra area paths filter them - i.e. intra area paths from this range are not advertised into other areas.

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> ipv6 cost <number>
cmd: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> ipv6 cost <number>
desc: OSPFv3 — This command sets link cost for the specified interface. The cost value is set to router-LSA’s metric field and used for SPF calculation.

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> dead-interval <number>
desc: OSPFv3 — Set number of seconds for router Dead Interval timer value used for Wait Timer and Inactivity Timer.

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> hello-interval <number>

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> mtu-ignore

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> network <type>

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> priority <number>

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> passive
desc: OSPFv3 — This command specifies interface as passive. Passive interface advertises its address, but does not run the OSPF protocol (adjacencies are not formed and hello packets are not generated).

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> retransmit-interval <number>

title: set protocols ospfv3 interface <interface> transmit-delay <number>

title: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart [grace-period (1-1800)]

title: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart helper enable [router-id A.B.C.D]

title: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart helper lsa-check-disable

title: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart helper supported-grace-time

desc: OSPFv3 — Supports as HELPER for configured grace period.

title: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart helper planned-only
cmd: set protocols ospfv3 graceful-restart helper planned-only
desc: OSPFv3 — It helps to support as HELPER only for planned restarts. By default, it supports both planned and unplanned outages.

title: set protocols ospfv3 redistribute <route source>

cmd: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld last-member-query-count <1-255>

title: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld last-member-query-interval <100-6553500>
cmd: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld last-member-query-interval <100-6553500>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the MLD Last Listener Query Interval, in milliseconds, on the specified interface.** This setting determines how long the router waits between Last Listener Queries.

title: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld max-response-time <100-6553500>
cmd: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld max-response-time <100-6553500>

title: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld version <1-2>
cmd: set protocols pim6 interface <interface-name> mld version <1-2>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the MLD version on the specified interface.** The default version is 2.

title: set protocols igmp-proxy interface <interface> role <upstream | downstream>
cmd: set protocols igmp-proxy interface <interface> role <upstream | downstream>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the operational role for the specified IGMP proxy interface.** - upstream: Communicates with upstream multicast sources to retrieve the multicast traffic.

title: set protocols igmp-proxy interface <interface> alt-subnet <network>
desc: Multicast — **Configure an allowed remote subnet for incoming multicast traffic on the specified IGMP proxy interface** By default, the IGMP proxy accepts multicast traffic only from directly connected subnets.

title: set protocols igmp-proxy interface <interface> whitelist <network>

title: set protocols igmp-proxy interface <interface> threshold <1-255>
desc: Multicast — **Configure the Time-to-Live (TTL) threshold for the specified IGMP proxy interface.** The IGMP proxy drops any multicast packet with a TTL value lower than the configured threshold.

title: set protocols igmp-proxy disable-quickleave

title: set protocols rip network <A.B.C.D/M>
desc: RIP — This command enables RIP and sets the RIP enable interface by NETWORK. The interfaces which have addresses matching with NETWORK are enabled.

title: set protocols rip interface <interface>

title: set protocols rip neighbor <A.B.C.D>
desc: BGP — This command specifies a RIP neighbor. When a neighbor doesn’t understand multicast, this command is used to specify neighbors.

title: set protocols rip default-distance <distance>

title: set protocols rip network-distance <A.B.C.D/M> distance <distance>
desc: RIP — This command sets default RIP distance to a specified value when the routes source IP address matches the specified prefix.

title: set protocols rip network-distance <A.B.C.D/M> access-list <name>
desc: VLAN — This command can be used with previous command to sets default RIP distance to specified value when the route source IP address matches the specified prefix and the specified access-list.

title: set protocols rip default-information originate
desc: RIP — This command generate a default route into the RIP.

title: set protocols rip distribute-list access-list <in|out> <number>

title: set protocols rip distribute-list interface <interface> access-list <in|out> <number>

title: set protocols rip distribute-list prefix-list <in|out> <name>

title: set protocols rip distribute-list interface <interface> prefix-list <in|out> <name>
cmd: set protocols rip distribute-list interface <interface> prefix-list <in|out> <name>
desc: ACL — This command allows you apply prefix lists to a chosen interface to filter the RIP path.

title: set protocols rip route <A.B.C.D/M>
desc: RIP — This command is specific to FRR and VyOS. The route command makes a static route only inside RIP.

title: set protocols rip timers update <seconds>
desc: RIP — This command specifies the update timer. Every update timer seconds, the RIP process is awakened to send an unsolicited response message containing the complete routing table to all neighboring RIP routers.

title: set protocols rip timers timeout <seconds>

title: set protocols rip default-metric <metric>

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> remote-as external
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> remote-as external
desc: BGP — Create a peer as you would when you specify an ASN, except that if the peers ASN is the same as mine as specified under the protocols bgp <asn> command the connection will be denied.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> shutdown

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> description <text>

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> update-source <address|interface>

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> capability dynamic

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> capability extended-nexthop
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> capability extended-nexthop

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> disable-capability-negotiation

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> override-capability
desc: BGP — This command allow override the result of Capability Negotiation with local configuration.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> strict-capability-match

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> password <text>

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> ttl-security hops <number>

desc: BGP — This command enforces Generalized TTL Security Mechanism (GTSM), as specified in 5082.

title: set protocols bgp peer-group <name>
desc: BGP — This command defines a new peer group. You can specify to the group the same parameters that you can specify for specific neighbors.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> peer-group <name>
desc: BGP — This command bind specific peer to peer group with a given name.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> network <prefix>
desc: BGP — This command is used for advertising IPv4 or IPv6 networks. :::{note} By default, the BGP prefix is advertised even if it's not present in the routing table.

title: set protocols bgp parameters network-import-check
desc: BGP — This configuration modifies the behavior of the network statement. If you have this configured the underlying network must exist in the routing table.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> aggregate-address <prefix>
desc: BGP — This command specifies an aggregate address. The router will also announce longer-prefixes inside of the aggregate address.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> aggregate-address <prefix> a…
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> aggregate-address <prefix> as-set
desc: BGP — This command specifies an aggregate address with a mathematical set of autonomous systems.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> aggregate-address <prefix> s…
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> aggregate-address <prefix> summary-only
desc: BGP — This command specifies an aggregate address and provides that longer-prefixes inside of the aggregate address are suppressed before sending BGP updates out to peers.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> unsuppress-map <name>
desc: BGP — This command applies route-map to selectively unsuppress prefixes suppressed by summarisation.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source>
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source>
desc: BGP — This command redistributes routing information from the given route source to the BGP process.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source>…
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source> metric <number>
desc: BGP — This command specifies metric (MED) for redistributed routes. The metric range is 0 to 4294967295.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source>…
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> redistribute <route source> route-map <name>
desc: BGP — This command allows to use route map to filter redistributed routes. There are six modes available for route source: connected, kernel, ospf, rip, static, table.

title: set protocols bgp parameters allow-martian-nexthop
desc: BGP — When a peer receives a martian nexthop as part of the NLRI for a route permit the nexthop to be used as such, instead of rejecting and resetting the connection.

title: set protocols bgp parameters router-id <id>
desc: BGP — This command specifies the router-ID. If router ID is not specified it will use the highest interface IP address.

title: set protocols bgp address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> maximum-paths <ebgp|ibgp> <n…
desc: BGP — This command defines the maximum number of parallel routes that the BGP can support.

title: set protocols bgp parameters no-hard-administrative-reset
desc: BGP — Do not send Hard Reset CEASE Notification for "Administrative Reset" events. When set and Graceful Restart Notification capability is exchanged between the peers, Graceful Restart procedures apply, and routes will be re…

title: set protocols bgp parameters log-neighbor-changes
desc: BGP — This command enable logging neighbor up/down changes and reset reason.

title: set protocols bgp parameters no-client-to-client-reflection
desc: BGP — This command disables route reflection between route reflector clients. By default, the clients of a route reflector are not required to be fully meshed and the routes from a client are reflected to other clients.

title: set protocols bgp parameters no-fast-external-failover
desc: BGP — Disable immediate session reset if peer's connected link goes down.

title: set protocols bgp parameters no-ipv6-auto-ra
desc: BGP — By default, FRR sends router advertisement packets when Extended Next Hop is on or when a connection is established directly using the device name (Unnumbered BGP).

title: set protocols bgp listen range <prefix> peer-group <name>
cmd: set protocols bgp listen range <prefix> peer-group <name>
desc: BGP — This command is useful if one desires to loosen the requirement for BGP to have strictly defined neighbors.

title: set protocols bgp listen limit <number>
desc: BGP — This command goes hand in hand with the listen range command to limit the amount of BGP neighbors that are allowed to connect to the local router.

title: set protocols bgp parameters ebgp-requires-policy
desc: BGP — This command changes the eBGP behavior of FRR. By default FRR enables 8212 functionality which affects how eBGP routes are advertised, namely no routes are advertised across eBGP sessions without some sort of egress rou…

title: set protocols bgp parameters labeled-unicast <explicit-null | ipv4-explicit-null | ipv6-e…
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters labeled-unicast <explicit-null | ipv4-explicit-null | ipv6-explicit-null>
desc: BGP — By default, locally advertised prefixes use the implicit-null label to encode in the outgoing NLRI.

title: set protocols bgp parameters distance global <external|internal|local> <distance>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters distance global <external|internal|local> <distance>
desc: BGP — This command change distance value of BGP. The arguments are the distance values for external routes, internal routes and local routes respectively.

title: set protocols bgp parameters distance prefix <subnet> distance <distance>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters distance prefix <subnet> distance <distance>
desc: BGP — This command sets the administrative distance for a particular route. The distance range is 1 to 255.

title: set protocols bgp timers holdtime <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command specifies hold-time in seconds. The timer range is 4 to 65535.

title: set protocols bgp timers keepalive <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command specifies keep-alive time in seconds. The timer can range from 4 to 65535.

title: set protocols bgp parameters update-delay max-delay <seconds>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters update-delay max-delay <seconds>
desc: BGP · protocols

title: set protocols bgp parameters update-delay establish-wait <seconds>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters update-delay establish-wait <seconds>
desc: BGP · protocols

title: set protocols bgp parameters dampening half-life <minutes>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters dampening half-life <minutes>

title: set protocols bgp parameters dampening re-use <seconds>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters dampening re-use <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command defines the accumulated penalty amount at which the route is re-advertised.

title: set protocols bgp parameters dampening start-suppress-time <seconds>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters dampening start-suppress-time <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command defines the accumulated penalty amount at which the route is suppressed.

title: set protocols bgp parameters dampening max-suppress-time <seconds>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters dampening max-suppress-time <seconds>
desc: BGP — This command defines the maximum time in minutes that a route is suppressed. The timer range is 1 to 255 minutes.

title: set protocols bgp parameters always-compare-med
desc: BGP — This command provides to compare the MED on routes, even when they were received from different neighbouring ASes.

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path confed
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path confed
desc: BGP — This command specifies that the length of confederation path sets and sequences should be taken into account during the BGP best path decision process.

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path multipath-relax
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path multipath-relax
desc: BGP — This command specifies that BGP decision process should consider paths of equal AS_PATH length candidates for multipath computation.

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path ignore
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath as-path ignore
desc: BGP — Ignore AS_PATH length when selecting a route

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath compare-routerid
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath compare-routerid
desc: BGP — Ensure that when comparing routes where both are equal on most metrics, including local-pref, AS_PATH length, IGP cost, MED, that the tie is broken based on router-ID.

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath med confed
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath med confed
desc: BGP — This command specifies that BGP considers the MED when comparing routes originated from different sub-ASs within the confederation to which this BGP speaker belongs.

title: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath med missing-as-worst
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters bestpath med missing-as-worst
desc: BGP — This command specifies that a route with a MED is always considered to be better than a route without a MED by causing the missing MED attribute to have a value of infinity.

title: set protocols bgp parameters default local-pref <local-pref value>
cmd: set protocols bgp parameters default local-pref <local-pref value>
desc: BGP — This command specifies the default local preference value. The local preference range is 0 to 4294967295.

title: set protocols bgp parameters deterministic-med
desc: BGP — This command provides to compare different MED values that advertised by neighbours in the same AS for routes selection.

title: set protocols bgp address-family ipv4-unicast network <prefix> backdoor
cmd: set protocols bgp address-family ipv4-unicast network <prefix> backdoor
desc: BGP — This command allows the router to prefer route to specified prefix learned via IGP through backdoor link instead of a route to the same prefix learned via EBGP.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> prefix-list <export|import> <name>
desc: BGP — This command applies the prfefix list filters named in \<name\> to the specified BGP neighbor to restrict the routing information that BGP learns and/or advertises.

cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> route-map <export|import> <name>
desc: BGP — This command applies the route map named in \<name\> to the specified BGP neighbor to control and modify routing information that is exchanged between peers.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> filter-list <export|import> <name>
desc: BGP — This command applies the AS path access list filters named in \<name\> to the specified BGP neighbor to restrict the routing information that BGP learns and/or advertises.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast>…
cmd: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> capability orf <receive|send>
desc: BGP — This command enables the ORF capability (described in 5291) on the local router, and enables ORF capability advertisement to the specified BGP peer.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address|interface> solo
desc: BGP — This command prevents from sending back prefixes learned from the neighbor.

title: set protocols bgp neighbor <address> address-family <ipv4-unicast|ipv6-unicast> route-ref…

title: set protocols bgp parameters cluster-id <id>
